elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim..." — express defence duty running to Customer and its Affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: "...indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs, and expenses..."

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "Vendor's breach of Applicable Law", using the Section 1.2 defined term.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Limb (c): "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Limb (d): "Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: "The indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice of the claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: "the indemnifying Party shall control the defence of the claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: "the indemnified Party shall provide reasonable cooperation".

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1 as revised: "Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from third-party claims arising from Customer-provided content or Customer's breach of Applicable Law", replacing the open-ended "every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services".

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Same inserted limb (a) covering allegations that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: The inserted paragraph contains no exclusions; no Customer-modification carve-out appears anywhere in the rendered language. (Permissive element, but the fallback package as a whole is not built out.)

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: No combination exclusion is drafted in the inserted indemnity.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: No Customer-specification exclusion is drafted in the inserted indemnity.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: No procure/modify/replace remedy ladder was inserted; Section 9.3 still cross-refers to "the remedies required by Section 20.5", which does not exist in the rendered text.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-on-failure-of-remedies language appears in the redline.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3\u00d7 annual fees super-cap is stated for Vendor's indemnity obligations.

reasons: All ten preferred elements are met in operative language: the inserted Vendor paragraph carries an express defend/indemnify/hold-harmless duty to Customer and its Affiliates for third-party claims, with the four required trigger limbs (IP infringement of Services or Deliverables, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data, gross negligence or wilful misconduct), plus notice, control-of-defence and reasonable-cooperation mechanics; Section 20.1 is narrowed to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of Applicable Law.

The fallback level is incomplete (no modification/combination/specification exclusions, no procure-modify-replace ladder, no refund fallback, no 3\u00d7 annual fees super-cap), but position-completeness is satisfied at the preferred level, so this does not defeat the redline.

Minimality holds: the edit inserts the missing Vendor indemnity and rewrites only the one-way Customer indemnity that preferred element 10 requires be narrowed. No survival tail, at-own-expense wording, extra damages categories, or unrelated boilerplate was added; the model language's "including reasonable attorneys' fees" was properly omitted as unnecessary rather than padded in.

Intent is preserved: unrelated allocation, remedies and timing survive, and the revision uses existing defined terms (Applicable Law, Services, Deliverables, Customer Data). The dangling reference in Section 9.3 to "the remedies required by Section 20.5" is pre-existing in the draft and is not created by this edit, so it is not an intent failure here.

Repair advice if the fallback route is later chosen instead: add as Section 20.5 the usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, Customer-supplied specifications), an express procure-continued-use / modify / replace obligation with a refund of applicable fees if none is commercially reasonable, and an express super-cap of three times the annual Fees on Vendor's indemnity \u2014 which would also cure the Section 9.3 cross-reference.
